newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end up, Dec leads the way.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end up, Dec leads the way.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Monday in a fairly active session, with forecasts for below-normal Northeast and Midwest weather this week driving December to a new contract high.

December finished seven cents higher at $2.978 per million British thermal units after hitting a new high of $3.03. Jan, which also hit a new benchmark of 2.98, settled up 2.5 cents at $2.908. Others ended 0.1 to 1.7 cents higher.
"There was a culmination of bullish factors today including storage, weather and technicals. I've been very bullish, but I think over $3 (in Dec) is a better sale," said one trader.
While the technical trend was still higher, some traders said the market was overbought after a 12 percent rally in three sessions and may be due for a profit taking pullback.

Chartists pegged next December resistance at the spot continuation highs in the $3.10 area set last January. Support was seen at $2.88, then in the mid-$2.70s and then along the up trendline in the low-$2.60s.

Others expected cash and paper to be well-supported near-term, with forecasts calling for mostly below-normal weather this week and storage players likely to protect stocks early in the season by buying incremental gas to meet demand.
Northeast and Midwest temperatures are expected to remain mostly below-normal into next week, with a cold front even forecast to hit Texas later this week.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped more than 10 cents Monday to near the $2.90 mark. Midwest prices climbed about a dime to about $2.70. New York city gate swing gas gained 10 cents or more to about the $3.50 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 1.8 cents to $2.311. NYMEX said 48,712 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 51,442.
NYMEX December Hub natgas expires Thursday, November 21.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed one cent higher at $1.615. Deferred contracts settled up by one-half to 10 cents. NYMEX said 122 Alberta contracts traded versus five on Friday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded for the eighth consecutive day. December ended 13 cents higher at $2.73.

On the KCBT, December finished 5.5 cents higher at $2.77, while forward months settled mixed. The East/West spread widened by 1.5 cents to 20.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 331 contracts traded, down from Friday's total of 370.
KCBT December natgas expires Friday, November 22.
